title: Can the Letters Make a Palindrome?

concept.title: At most one letter with an odd count
body: A palindrome reads the same backwards. Its letters come in **pairs** around the middle, and in an odd-length palindrome the middle letter is alone. So the letters of a word can be rearranged into a palindrome exactly when **at most one letter occurs an odd number of times**.
A neat trick with a set: toggle each letter (add it if absent, remove it if present). The letters left in the set are exactly the letters with an odd count.

statement: Print `yes` if the letters of the word can be rearranged to form a palindrome (a word that reads the same forwards and backwards), otherwise print `no`. Upper and lower case letters are different.

examples.note: racecar uses the letters of carrace.
Four letters that occur once each.

hints: Count how often each letter occurs.
In a palindrome at most one letter can have an odd count (the middle one).
Count the letters with an odd count and compare with 1.

explanation: A set toggled by every letter ends up holding the letters with an odd count. A palindrome needs at most one of them.
